Subject: RE: MSA + Order Form - liability carve-out and security addendum

Jonas / Marcus —

I reviewed the redlines and Grace’s request. High-level recommendations below before we send a formal counter:

1) Sub-limit amount: propose Redwood counter of USD 750,000 as a breach-specific cap for direct losses arising from a security incident, applicable per incident and aggregate per 12-month period. This is a middle ground between a low six-figure ask and unlimited exposure.

2) Scope & definitions: tie the sub-limit to a narrow definition of "Security Incident" (as defined in the Security Addendum) and exclude (a) general business interruption claims not causally linked to a compromise of customer data, and (b) third-party claims arising from customer contracts where those contracts allocate responsibility elsewhere.

3) Carve-outs and exclusions: keep consequential, punitive, and exemplary damages excluded generally, but allow an exception where required by statute. Also carve out liability for willful misconduct and gross negligence (these remain uncapped).

4) Cooperation and remedies: require Grace to follow the incident response steps in the Security Addendum (timely notification, forensics access, joint mitigation decisions). Limit Redwood’s obligation to reasonable cooperation and reimbursement of reasonable out-of-pocket forensic costs where Redwood’s systems are at fault.

5) Insurance & indemnity: add a paragraph requiring Redwood to maintain cyber insurance with limits no less than USD 5M and to provide a certificate on renewal; this reduces residual risk and supports the proposed sub-limit.

6) Contract mechanics: Security Addendum must be expressly incorporated into the Order Form by reference and signed appendices; otherwise the sub-limit language is unenforceable.

I’ll draft redline text reflecting the above and attach it to an email. Marcus — note that 750k is likely to be a pricing / commercial ask; if Grace insists on a lower number we should consider a price uplift or professional services credit to offset exposure.

Laura Bennett
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.example.com

Thanks Laura —

A few quick commercial points to keep in mind for the counter:

- Deal size / ARR: Grace is in our mid-market band (~$280k ARR). A 750k breach cap is 2.7x ARR; that’s defendable given cyber insurance and our controls, but it may exceed their procurement comfort.
- Trade-offs: happy to offer a two-tier approach — 1) standard breach sub-limit at $500k with a contractual option to increase to $750k if Grace purchases the premium support package or agrees to a 12-month upfront commit; or 2) accept 750k but include a liability-sharing mechanism for third-party consumer claims.
- Escalation: if legal stalls, I’m prepared to bring up to my manager and offer a one-time onboarding credit in exchange for the higher sub-limit.

If everyone’s ok, I suggest we send the counter with both concrete numbers and a commercial option explained (support/commit trade). Saves back-and-forth and leaves Grace a path to close quickly.

Thanks for the redlines and for flagging the procurement requirement. Per our internal review, Redwood can accept a breach-specific sub-limit that is explicitly tied to the Security Addendum, provided the following is agreed: 

1) Sub-limit: Redwood proposes a breach-specific cap of USD 750,000 per Security Incident and USD 1,500,000 aggregate in any rolling 12-month period.

2) Alternate commercial path: if Grace prefers lower exposure, we can offer USD 500,000 per incident (USD 1,000,000 aggregate) in exchange for either (a) enrolling in Redwood Premium Support for the first 12 months of the Agreement, or (b) a 12-month upfront payment on the first year (standard discount withheld).

3) Security Addendum tie-in: the Security Addendum must be executed as Appendix B of the Order Form and will define "Security Incident," notification timelines, forensics cooperation, and remediation steps. Redwood’s obligations are limited to reasonable cooperation and remediation where Redwood systems caused the incident; willful misconduct and gross negligence remain uncapped.

4) Insurance: Redwood will provide evidence of cyber insurance with limits of not less than USD 5,000,000 and will update the certificate on annual renewal.

5) Next steps: Laura attached a redline to the Security Addendum and a short MSA/Order Form redline that implements the cap language and incorporation mechanics. Please review and let us know whether Grace prefers the $750k path or the $500k + premium-support/commit option. We’re available for a 30-minute call Wednesday to finalize.

Looking forward to wrapping this up quickly — we’re eager to get Grace onboarded.

Best regards,
